# Stylized-ImageNet and the texture–shape cue conflict — the shortcut named, measured, and removed by data alone

**Geirhos et al. 2019.** Two artefacts and one result. The artefacts: a **cue-conflict stimulus set** (1,280 images whose shape says *cat* and whose texture says *elephant*, generated by style transfer) and **Stylized-ImageNet (SIN)**, ImageNet with every image's texture replaced by the style of a random painting. The result: ImageNet-trained convolutional networks classify by local texture, humans by global shape, and *the same ResNet-50* flips to shape when the texture is made uninformative — so the wiki's canonical shortcut is **induced by training data, not by architecture**. This is the primary source behind the texture rows on [[wiki/concepts/shortcut-learning.md]] and the Stylized-ImageNet number on [[wiki/entities/imagenet-c.md]].

---

## The instrument: a shift under which both candidate rules stay correct

Every other o.o.d. instrument in the wiki degrades an input and reports lost accuracy, which conflates *which feature the rule reads* with *how hard the input got*. A cue conflict does neither: the image carries two intact, mutually exclusive class labels, so the model's **response identity** reads out the feature its rule uses, at full accuracy, with no ground truth needed beyond the two source classes.

| Element | Choice | Why it is load-bearing |
|---|---|---|
| Stimulus | Iterative style transfer (Gatys et al. 2016), texture image as style, object image as content; 1,280 images, 80 per category | Natural image statistics preserved, so a failure cannot be blamed on domain shift the way silhouettes and edge maps can |
| Label space | 16-class-ImageNet (airplane … truck), 1,000 ImageNet classes mapped up through WordNet | Makes human and network responses directly comparable on the same images |
| Human protocol | 300 ms fixation → **200 ms** stimulus → **200 ms 1/f pink-noise mask** → 1,500 ms 4×4 icon response grid | The mask truncates recurrent/feedback processing, making the comparison to a feedforward network fair rather than flattering to the human |
| Instruction | "click on the object category that you see; there is no right or wrong answer" | Shape/texture-neutral, so the human shape bias is not an artefact of task framing |
| Item selection | Only source objects and textures **all four networks already classified correctly** | Removes the "the network just could not see it" explanation from the decisive experiment |
| Scale | 9 experiments, 48,560 trials, 97 observers | |

**Preliminary experiments (no conflict), same 16 categories:** original colour ≈ greyscale ≈ texture-only — humans and networks alike near ceiling; **silhouette** and **Canny edge** versions — networks far below humans. Shape-only inputs are where networks fall over, and the authors concede the domain-shift confound there, which is exactly what the cue-conflict design removes.

## Result 1 — the bias, and it worsens as architectures improve

Fraction of shape vs. texture responses on cue-conflict images:

| Observer | Shape | Texture |
|---|---|---|
| **Humans** | **95.9%** | 4.1% |
| AlexNet | 42.9% | 57.1% |
| GoogLeNet | 31.2% | 68.8% |
| ResNet-50 | 22.1% | 77.9% |
| VGG-16 | 17.2% | 82.8% |
| ResNet-50 trained on **SIN** | **81%** | 19% |

**The ordering is the finding the paper does not dwell on and the wiki should:** shape bias falls roughly monotonically from AlexNet to the more accurate, more ventral-stream-predictive networks. Architecture progress measured by ImageNet accuracy bought *more* texture reliance, which is the same shape of result as `Relative mCE` never improving while `mCE` fell across the same six years ([[wiki/entities/imagenet-c.md]], `F15`) — **two independent instruments saying accuracy progress and rule-quality progress came apart in the same period.**

## Result 2 — Stylized-ImageNet, and the transfer asymmetry

SIN construction: AdaIN (Adaptive Instance Normalization) fast style transfer at stylization coefficient `α = 1.0`, style drawn from 79,434 paintings (Kaggle *Painter by Numbers*); each source image stylized **once**. A *different* stylization method from the one used to build the cue-conflict test set, so the evaluation does not measure one style-transfer implementation's fingerprint.

Top-5 accuracy, `train → test`:

| Architecture | IN→IN | IN→SIN | SIN→SIN | SIN→IN |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ResNet-50 | 92.9 | **16.4** | 79.0 | **82.6** |
| BagNet-33 | 86.4 | 4.2 | 48.9 | 53.0 |
| BagNet-17 | 80.3 | 2.5 | 29.3 | 32.6 |
| BagNet-9 | 70.0 | 1.4 | 10.0 | 10.9 |

Two things fall out:

- **The asymmetry `16.4` vs `82.6` is the general claim.** A texture representation transfers to a shape task not at all; a shape representation transfers to the texture-solvable task almost intact, **with no fine-tuning**. The non-shortcut rule is not a robustness/accuracy trade at the representation level — it *subsumes* the shortcut rule. Whatever the shortcut buys is bought at training time (SIN is harder: 79.0 vs 92.9), not held at test time.
- **The BagNet rows are a dataset-validation design worth stealing.** BagNets are ResNet-50s with the receptive field clamped to 9×9 / 17×17 / 33×33 pixels, so they *cannot* use long-range spatial relations. They reach 70–86 top-5 on ImageNet — proof that ImageNet is texture-solvable — and collapse to 10.0–48.9 on SIN. **A benchmark claiming to have removed a shortcut should ship an architecture-side control that is structurally incapable of the intended rule, and show it fails.** ImageNet-C's held-out corruption split governs the *choice among shifts*; this governs whether the shift removed what it claims.

## Result 3 — the shape representation is free, and then some

| Model | Training | Fine-tune | top-1 IN | top-5 IN | Pascal VOC 2007 mAP50 | MS COCO mAP50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vanilla ResNet-50 | IN | — | 76.13 | 92.86 | 70.7 | 52.3 |
| | SIN | — | 60.18 | 82.62 | 70.6 | 51.9 |
| | SIN+IN | — | 74.59 | 92.14 | 74.0 | 53.8 |
| **Shape-ResNet** | SIN+IN | IN | **76.72** | **93.28** | **75.1** | **55.2** |

- SIN **alone** costs 16 points of top-1 — the shortcut is worth real i.i.d. accuracy, and any honest statement of the data lever's price is this row, not the last one.
- SIN **as augmentation**, with an IN fine-tune, is strictly better than vanilla on every column: accuracy, detection (+4.4 VOC, +2.9 COCO), and robustness. Detection gains are mechanistically expected — a bounding box is aligned with global shape, not with texture.
- **Robustness never trained for:** SIN-trained networks beat IN-trained on uniform noise, contrast, high-pass, phase noise and all three eidolon families, approaching human distortion tolerance. On ImageNet-C, SIN+IN improves **13 of 15** corruptions and takes mCE **76.7 → 69.3** ([[wiki/entities/imagenet-c.md]]).
- **The one exception is diagnostic:** low-pass filtering / blur gets *worse*, attributed to SIN's over-representation of high-frequency painting detail and reliance on sharp edges. A declared nuisance direction is also a declared *reliance* — removing texture installed an edge dependency nobody asked for. `(brainstorm)` The general form: an augmentation that blocks shortcut A does not return a rule that reads nothing; it returns the next-cheapest sufficient rule, whose own failure surface is unmeasured unless the shift family is broad enough to catch it. This is the argument for held-out shift families rather than for any particular augmentation.

## What this settles, and what it does not

| Claim | Status after this paper |
|---|---|
| Convolutional networks build increasingly complex *shape* representations (the "shape hypothesis") | **Falsified as a description of ImageNet-trained networks** — and it was the standard textbook account, held by the field's own reviews |
| The texture bias is architectural | **No.** Same architecture, same optimiser, different data → 22% → 81% shape bias. Pure data lever ([[wiki/empirical-tensions.md]] T15) |
| ImageNet measures object recognition | **No** — it measures a task local texture statistics suffice for, which is the wiki's canonical "dataset ≠ ability" case |
| Networks are good models of the ventral stream | **Weakened**: their predictive power for ventral-stream responses may rest on human-like *texture* representations rather than contour representations — matched neural predictivity with an unmatched strategy ([[wiki/concepts/neuroscience-ai-transfer.md]]) |
| Shape bias is *the* fix | Not established. SIN raises shape bias to 81% and human is 95.9%; nothing here shows shape is the intended rule in general, only that it is the intended rule for these categories |

**Limitations to carry.** (i) 16 coarse categories, one modality, one shortcut — the method generalises, the artefact does not. (ii) The cue-conflict read-out needs a *nameable pair* of competing features; most shortcuts are not nameable in advance, which is why this instrument does not close `G17`. (iii) Style transfer's "shape" is the content image's, so the design inherits whatever the style-transfer decomposition counts as content. (iv) The human 95.9% is measured under a backward mask that suppresses feedback; the unmasked human bias could be higher still, which would widen the gap rather than narrow it.

## Connections

- **[[wiki/concepts/error-consistency.md]]** — the second question these same trials answer. The cue-conflict, edge and silhouette responses were collected to read out *which feature* a model uses; run through chance-discounted trial-by-trial agreement they show that sixteen ImageNet networks are near-independent of human observers (`κ` .066–.080 against human↔human .331) and near-identical to each other (up to .793), so the texture finding is not one model's bias but the field's single shared strategy. These stimuli are also what makes the measurement possible at all — `κ` is undefined at ceiling, and the out-of-distribution sets are what move both parties into the measurable band (T307).
- **[[wiki/concepts/shortcut-learning.md]]** — the primary source for that page's canonical example, and its cleanest demonstration of the data lever: the shortcut is removed by construction (make texture uninformative) with architecture, loss and optimiser untouched, taking shape bias 22% → 81% and mCE 76.7 → 69.3, while adding *more* ImageNet data would not have moved either.
- **[[wiki/entities/imagenet-c.md]]** — the corruption-side price of the same shortcut and the same period-level story from the other direction: shape bias falls AlexNet → ResNet-50 while `Relative mCE` fails to improve over the identical model sequence, so two unrelated instruments agree that ImageNet accuracy progress was not rule progress.
- **[[wiki/concepts/certification-instruments.md]]** — supplies `I28`, the cue-conflict read-out: a shift under which *both* candidate rules remain correct, so response identity rather than accuracy loss identifies which feature the decision rule reads, plus the BagNet capacity control that validates a shortcut-removing dataset.
- **[[wiki/concepts/neuroscience-ai-transfer.md]]** — the concrete instance of the same-strategy fallacy on the reverse channel: networks that match human accuracy on undistorted images and predict ventral-stream responses are shown, on the same images, to be running a different classification strategy from the humans they model.
- **[[wiki/concepts/latent-graph-discovery.md]]** — hardness source 5 made visible: texture and shape are two edges equally consistent with ImageNet, the objective selects the cheaper one, and only an environment in which the cheap edge is broken by construction reveals which was recovered.
- **[[wiki/concepts/environment-invariance.md]]** — SIN is the crude, non-parametric version of the same move: rather than penalise environment-varying classifiers, author one environment in which the spurious feature carries no signal at all; it needs no environment labels and no invariance penalty, and it works, at the cost of requiring the shortcut to be named in advance.
- **[[wiki/entities/objectnet.md]]** — the same year's answer to the same question from the opposite end of the nameability axis, and the reason this page's limitation (ii) matters: a cue conflict returns *which* feature the rule reads but needs both features named in advance, while control-at-capture varies rotation, viewpoint and context — nuisance variables whose effect on the rule is never identified — and returns only a magnitude (40–45%), which is the trade the wiki's o.o.d. instruments have not escaped.
- **[[wiki/entities/mae.md]]** — the same high-frequency band read with the opposite sign: texture is the nameable nuisance whose removal buys 22% → 81% shape bias here, and is part of the reconstruction target whose PCA-truncation *costs* a masked auto-encoder 1.2 linear points there — so what is a shortcut for a discriminative classifier is training signal for a generative one, and "discard the unpredictable detail" is dataset-dependent rather than principled (T162).
